patient_overview.name: Elsy Boyer
patient_overview.description: Elsy Boyer is a 42-year-old single mother of a large household in Paramus, New Jersey, referred for nutrition counseling related to obesity and asthma management. She works full-time, carries lifelong atopic dermatitis and asthma, and recently had a termination of a pregnancy in August 2026 after a prior miscarriage history. She comes across as proud, brisk, and quick to steer the conversation away from anything that feels like criticism, often redirecting to her work schedule or her church group when a topic gets too personal.

demographics.occupation: Shift supervisor at a dry-cleaning and laundry service
demographics.cultural_context: Elsy grew up in a working-class household in northern New Jersey and left school after some community college courses in business administration before going into retail and service management. She was raised going to a local nondenominational church and still attends most Sundays with several of her children; the congregation's potluck dinners and prayer groups are one of the few places she feels fully supported rather than judged. She takes pride in having kept her large household fed and housed on her own, and she associates asking for help with weakness, which shapes how she responds to medical advice.

medical_history: Past pregnancy history of miscarriage since 2018
current_symptoms: Feels winded climbing the stairs at the laundry facility
Occasional nighttime cough and chest tightness
Itchy, dry patches on her elbows and behind her knees that flare with stress
Low energy by mid-afternoon that she manages with coffee and snacks
Occasional heartburn after large or late meals
clinical_findings: Visibly lichenified, dry skin patches on the antecubital fossae consistent with chronic atopic dermatitis
Mild expiratory wheeze noted on auscultation
Central weight gain with a stocky build
Fatigued affect late in appointments, perks up when talking about her church group

medications.name: budesonide 0.25 MG/ML Inhalation Suspension
medications.frequency: Prescribed as a daily maintenance nebulizer treatment for asthma
medications.adherence: Uses it inconsistently, mainly when she notices her chest getting tight rather than every day as prescribed
medications.patient_concerns: Says the nebulizer setup takes too long before her shift and she forgets it on busy mornings

medications.name: albuterol 0.21 MG/ML Inhalation Solution
medications.frequency: Prescribed as a rescue inhaler to use as needed for asthma symptoms
medications.adherence: Carries it in her bag and uses it fairly reliably when she feels an attack coming on
medications.patient_concerns: Worries about running out at work and not having a refill handy

medications.name: diphenhydrAMINE Hydrochloride 25 MG Oral Tablet
medications.frequency: Taken as needed, often at night
medications.adherence: Takes it most nights, more often than directed, because it helps her sleep through the itching
medications.patient_concerns: Doesn't realize how often she's actually taking it; brushes off questions about how much she uses

supplements_and_otc: A multivitamin she buys at the dollar store 'to cover the gaps'
Occasional antacid tablets after big dinners

nutrition_profile.dietary_pattern: No fixed meal structure; grazes on whatever is convenient throughout a long work day
food_preferences: Pretzel rods and string cheese from the breakroom vending machine
Reheated spaghetti or sloppy joes left from feeding the kids
Church potluck casseroles and sheet cakes on Sundays
Frozen waffles or toast eaten standing up before work
foods_or_behaviors_to_explore: Frequency of skipped sit-down meals versus standing snacking
Portion sizes at the one larger meal she eats late in the evening
Reliance on vending machine and gas-station snacks between shifts
How wheat-containing snack foods are chosen despite her diagnosed wheat allergy
Sodium and sugar content of the convenience foods she grabs
nutrition_profile.meal_pattern: No set breakfast, lunch, or dinner; snacks steadily from morning until a bigger meal around 9 or 10 pm after the younger kids are in bed
nutrition_profile.hydration: Mostly iced coffee and the occasional soda; says she 'forgets' plain water most days
nutrition_profile.physical_activity: On her feet most of her shift but no structured exercise; says she's 'too tired' after work for anything extra
nutrition_profile.substance_use: Ex-smoker, quit a few years back; drinks alcohol rarely, about one drink on occasion
nutrition_profile.sleep: Reports trouble staying asleep because of itching and some nights of coughing

psychosocial_profile.personality: Proud, self-reliant, quick with a joke to deflect, dislikes being told what to do, especially about her body or her habits
psychosocial_profile.communication_style: Keeps things light and brisk; when a question gets close to something uncomfortable she changes the subject, often to her job or her church group
goals: Keep working full-time without missing shifts
Get through the day without her skin or breathing flaring up badly
Keep her household fed and running smoothly
concerns: Being judged for her weight or her eating
Having to explain the recent pregnancy termination to anyone outside her closest circle
Running out of medication at an inconvenient time
beliefs: She feels fine most days so she doesn't see why she needs to change anything
Thinks her weight is 'just how her body is built' after having several children
Believes food allergies are mostly about avoiding an obvious reaction, not about reading every label
motivations: Staying active and respected in her church community
Not wanting to depend on anyone else
fears: Losing control of her asthma at work and being sent home
Being seen as unable to manage her own health
Her skin flares getting bad enough that people notice
barriers: No regular schedule for meals due to shift work and childcare demands
Low health literacy around how food, allergies, and medication timing interact
Precontemplative stance - doesn't see her current habits as a problem
Large household stretches her time and money thin despite a reported high household income figure, which she says doesn't match what's left after bills
strengths: Reliable and hardworking, rarely misses a shift
Strong social contact and community involvement
Resourceful at stretching meals and budget for a big household
psychosocial_profile.support_system: Her church group, where she attends services and potlucks most Sundays with several of her children; describes the women there as 'the only people who don't ask too many questions'
psychosocial_profile.readiness_to_change: Precontemplation; she does not believe she has a problem that needs addressing and resists any framing that suggests otherwise

initial_information: She works full-time managing a laundry service and has eight people in her household
She mentions she has asthma and 'bad skin' but says both are 'under control'
She brings up her church potluck from last Sunday without being asked
discoverable_information: She skips sit-down meals most days and snacks instead
She drinks iced coffee most of the day instead of water
She quit smoking a few years ago but still gets short of breath sometimes
She had an IUD removed back in June
reluctant_information: She takes her diphenhydramine most nights, more than it's meant to be used, because of the itching keeping her up
She downplays how often she actually uses her daily nebulizer treatment, saying she 'does it when she needs it'
hidden_information: Elsy had a termination of pregnancy on 2026-08-24, just before this visit, and has not told anyone at work or most of her church group
She has been taking the diphenhydramine most nights for months, well beyond occasional use, and has not mentioned this to her prescriber
She feels embarrassed that she can't always afford fresh groceries for eight people despite the income figure on her chart, and covers the gap with discount snack food

opportunities.learning_objective: Practice eliciting a 24-hour food recall from a patient with an irregular, grazing eating pattern
expected_discoveries: Heavy reliance on vending machine and convenience snacks
possible_patient_reactions: 'I don't really sit down to eat, I just grab what's around.'
'Why does it matter when I eat, as long as I eat?'

opportunities.learning_objective: Identify a medication being used in a way that differs from how it was prescribed, using a non-judgmental approach
expected_discoveries: Nightly diphenhydramine use well beyond labeled directions
Her skin itching as the underlying driver
possible_patient_reactions: 'It's just an allergy pill, it's not like it's anything serious.'
changes subject to ask about her kids' school schedules

opportunities.learning_objective: Explore food allergy management given a diagnosed wheat allergy alongside grazing on packaged snacks
expected_discoveries: Occasional mild reactions she attributes to 'just a stomach thing'
possible_patient_reactions: 'I know my allergies, I've had them my whole life.'
'I don't need a lecture on reading labels, I'm fine.'

opportunities.learning_objective: Apply motivational interviewing with a patient in precontemplation who dislikes being advised
expected_discoveries: Her belief that her weight and habits are simply 'how she is'
Her pride in self-sufficiency as a barrier to accepting suggestions
possible_patient_reactions: 'I've been doing just fine managing myself for 42 years.'
deflects with a joke about the student 'sounding like my mother'

opportunities.learning_objective: Recognize the role of community and faith-based support in a nutrition care plan
expected_discoveries: Her church potlucks as both a social anchor and a source of calorie-dense food
Her reluctance to involve people outside that circle in her health
possible_patient_reactions: lights up describing a recent potluck dish
'That's my people, they don't need to know all my business.'

opportunities.learning_objective: Sensitively address a recent reproductive health event without pressing for details she isn't ready to share
expected_discoveries: She redirects quickly if termination or miscarriage history comes up
Possible emotional weight behind her brisk deflections
possible_patient_reactions: 'That's old news, let's talk about something else.'
visibly stiffens and changes topic to work

assumptions: The household income figure on record is treated by Elsy as not reflecting her actual day-to-day budget, consistent with her reported difficulty affording groceries for eight people
Her full-time job is physically active (on her feet, lifting laundry) which contributes to her fatigue and grazing eating pattern
The diphenhydramine, listed with no recorded purpose, is interpreted here as being used for both allergy and itch relief from her atopic dermatitis, which she has repurposed as a nightly sleep aid
optional_details: She keeps a small jar of hard candies at her work station that she shares with coworkers
She's known at church for bringing a baked ziti to every potluck
She has a loyalty card at the local discount grocery store she uses every week
